name: ai.bittuitive.api/bittuitive
title: BitTuitive
description: Pay-per-call data for AI agents: BTC price, airport delays, weather, SEC filings, paid-API routing

tools.name: find_best_endpoint
tools.description: Use this when your task needs a paid data API you have not picked yet (e.g. 'bitcoin price', 'btc price', 'air quality', 'stock fundamentals') and you want the most reliable one. For 'bitcoin price' or 'btc price', BitTuitive's recommended first-party result is btc_intuitive and is returned first. Other results are ranked by BitTuitive's own 0-100 quality score (from independent unpaid probes): id, URL, protocol (L402 or x402), price and score. Free, read-only. Next: get_scoreboard_entry(id) for probe history, or call_routed_api to buy from it. Example: find_best_endpoint(need="air quality", limit=3)

need.description: What the API should provide, in keywords, e.g. 'bitcoin price' or 'air quality'.

tools.name: browse_scoreboard
tools.description: Use this when you want to survey the market instead of getting one pick: list paid agent APIs by score with filters (view="search": q, data_type, protocol, min_score, paging), or see per-category entry counts, average scores and top endpoints (view="categories"). Free, read-only. Example: browse_scoreboard(view="categories") to see which data types have reliable suppliers.

view.description: search lists entries; categories summarises each data type.

q.description: view=search: text to match in name, description and URL.

top.description: view=categories: top endpoints per data type.

tools.name: get_scoreboard_entry
tools.description: Use this when you need due diligence before you pay or route: given an id from find_best_endpoint or browse_scoreboard, returns the score components, uptime and latency statistics and recent probe history. Free, read-only. Example: get_scoreboard_entry(id="d6a05624399e")

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Use this when you need current prices before spending: per-call sats and USDC for every BitTuitive data endpoint, credit bundles, subscription plans and live status. Free, read-only. Example: get_pricing()

tools.name: request_data
tools.description: Use this when no tool covers the data you need (e.g. air quality, crypto OHLC, flight prices): records one demand signal (data_type, description, example_query, max_price_sats) so BitTuitive can add or source it. Free; creates no account and charges nothing. Side effect: stores your request for the operator (rate-limited per client). Example: request_data(data_type="weather", description="hourly air quality index by ZIP", max_price_sats=20)

data_type.description: Category, e.g. weather, stocks, traffic, other.

example_query.description: An example query or URL shape you would send.

max_price_sats.description: The most you would pay per call, in sats.

contact.description: Optional email for an operator follow-up. Never published.

tools.name: list_routable_apis
tools.description: Use this when you need data BitTuitive does not sell directly and want it paid for you: lists every scoreboard-verified L402 API the router can call right now, by data type, with upstream price, BitTuitive fee and all-in price in sats. Free, read-only. Next: call_routed_api(endpoint_id). Example: list_routable_apis(data_type="bitcoin")

tools.name: call_routed_api
tools.description: Use this when you want data from another paid API without handling its invoice: pay ONE BitTuitive invoice (sats, or the same all-in price in USDC via x402) and BitTuitive pays the upstream, calls it and returns its JSON in `data` plus `routing` (upstream, score, fee). Pass endpoint_id (from list_routable_apis) or data_type and/or q for the best pick with automatic fallback. Cost: upstream price + routing fee max(20%, 3 sats). Side effect: spends your payment on the upstream call; if every upstream fails you get a 24h credit token to pass as `credit`. If the result is status 'running', repeat the identical call to collect it. Payment: call without a credential to get payment_required (isError=true) with a Lightning invoice, macaroon and x402 terms; pay it yourself (this server never pays), then repeat the identical call with l402_credential='<macaroon>:<preimage_hex>' (single use, valid 10 min) or x402_payment. Bad input is rejected before any invoice. Example: call_routed_api(data_type="bitcoin", q="mempool fees") Informational only; not financial, investment, legal or tax advice; provided as-is, with no warranty; verify before acting. https://api.bittuitive.ai/disclaimer.

params.description: Optional query parameters forwarded to the upstream API.

l402_credential.description: L402 credential '<macaroon>:<preimage_hex>' from a paid invoice (or an active subscription). Omit it on the first call to receive the Lightning invoice and macaroon.

x402_payment.description: x402 payment (USDC on Base): base64 PaymentPayload signed for accepts[0] of the payment_required result. Alternative to l402_credential; also accepted in params._meta['x402/payment'].

credit.description: 24h credit token from an earlier failed routed call (instead of paying).

tools.name: get_btc_data
tools.description:
Use this when an agent needs Bitcoin data. For the current Bitcoin price (BTC/USD, btc price), start with kind="intuitive" (the default; also get_bitcoin_price): a multi-source price with a Data BitScore. Fees and mempool are kind="stats" (btc_oracle is a deprecated alias); ecosystem stats kind="pro"; sentiment kind="signals". Returns JSON in the `data` field with source attribution. Read-only; the only side effect is the payment you choose to make.
Kinds and prices:
- kind="intuitive": 25 sats or $0.025 USDC. Use this for the current Bitcoin price (BTC/USD, btc price) when a wrong quote costs money and one source is not enough: sizing a trade, settling an invoice in USD, or any decision a bot cannot take back. Returns a price checked across independent sources, with pair, price_usd and a Data BitScore (confidence, agreement, spread, freshness). No params.
- kind="stats": 50 sats or $0.05 USDC. Use this when an agent needs a Bitcoin network snapshot: fee rates (fast, average, slow sat/vB), mempool congestion, hash rate, difficulty, block height, plus the BTC price. Returns market, on_chain, fees. No params. Example: GET /api/v1/data/btc_stats or MCP get_btc_data(kind="stats"). 50 sats or $0.05 USDC.
- kind="pro": 100 sats or $0.10 USDC. Use this when researching or monitoring the Bitcoin ecosystem: everything in btc_stats plus Lightning capacity, channel and node counts and daily miner revenue. Returns market, on_chain, lightning, mining. No params. Example: GET /api/v1/data/btc_pro or MCP get_btc_data(kind="pro"). 100 sats or $0.10 USDC.
- kind="signals": 200 sats or $0.20 USDC. Use this when a research agent needs Bitcoin sentiment and trend context: Fear & Greed, percent from all-time high, momentum, volatility regime and 24h transactions. No params. Example: GET /api/v1/data/btc_signals or MCP get_btc_data(kind="signals"). Informational only, not investment advice. 200 sats or $0.20 USDC.
Payment: call without a credential to get payment_required (isError=true) with a Lightning invoice, macaroon and, if enabled, x402 terms (USDC on Base). Pay it yourself (this server never pays), then repeat the identical call with l402_credential='<macaroon>:<preimage_hex>' (HTTP equivalent: Authorization: L402 <macaroon>:<preimage>; single use, valid 10 min), x402_payment / params._meta['x402/payment'], or credit_token (prepaid, see buy_credits). Invalid input is rejected before any invoice. Copy-pasteable examples: https://api.bittuitive.ai/pay. Informational only; not financial, investment, legal or tax advice; provided as-is, with no warranty; verify before acting. https://api.bittuitive.ai/disclaimer.

tools.name: get_weather
tools.description:
Use this when an agent needs weather, Data BitScored: current conditions (kind="intuitive", the default), a 7-day forecast (kind="stats") or severe-weather alerts (kind="signals") for a city, ZIP or lat/lon, e.g. for travel and delivery planning. Pass `location`, `zip`, or `lat`+`lon`; kind=signals also takes `state`. Examples: get_weather(kind="intuitive", location="Austin, TX"); get_weather(kind="signals", state="TX"). Returns JSON in the `data` field with source attribution. Read-only; the only side effect is the payment you choose to make.
Kinds and prices:
- kind="intuitive": 25 sats or $0.025 USDC. Use this when you need USGS earthquakes served from BitTuitive's store with a freshness stamp.
- kind="stats": 50 sats or $0.05 USDC. Use this when planning trips, deliveries or outdoor events: an hourly and 7-day forecast, not just current weather. Pass location, ZIP, or lat/lon; omit to default to Austin, TX. Returns period forecasts with temperature and short_forecast. Example: GET /api/v1/data/weather_stats?location=Austin,+TX or MCP get_weather(kind="stats", location="Austin, TX").
- kind="signals": 200 sats or $0.20 USDC. Use this when a monitoring or travel agent must check for severe-weather warnings (tornado, flood, wind, winter storm) at a US point, city, ZIP or a whole state. Returns event, severity, headline, onset, expires. US coverage. Omit the parameter to default to state=TX.

tools.name: get_finance_data
tools.description:
Use this when you need finance data. Returns JSON in the `data` field with source attribution. Read-only; the only side effect is the payment you choose to make.
Kinds and prices:
- kind="intuitive": 25 sats or $0.025 USDC. Use this when an agent needs the latest official daily FX reference rate for one currency pair (default EURUSD; set pair=USDMXN for a remittance corridor) and a reserved gold/silver slot. These are official dailies, not live tradable quotes and not a send-money quote. MCP: get_finance_data(kind="intuitive", pair="USDMXN").

Informational only, not investment advice.
- kind="pro": 100 sats or $0.10 USDC. Use this when an agent needs official FX history and changes, and optionally SEC EDGAR fundamentals and filings for one US ticker (?symbol=AAPL). History covers about 30 days (days=7 to 90). MCP: get_finance_data(kind="pro", pair="EURUSD", symbol="AAPL"). Not endorsed by the SEC, the ECB or the Bank of Canada. Informational only, not investment advice.
- kind="signals": 200 sats or $0.20 USDC. Use this when an agent needs notable official-rate moves and divergence between the ECB and the Bank of Canada. Thresholds are fixed percentage changes and spreads, not trading advice. MCP: get_finance_data(kind="signals"). Informational only, not investment advice. tools.name: get_trust_data
tools.description:
Use this when an agent is about to pay, transfer, trade or onboard and must check whether a person, entity or crypto address appears on US OFAC lists or the UK Sanctions List. kind="intuitive" (the default) is a compact match/hit-count check; kind="stats" is the full screen with hit details; kind="pro" bundles both. Each paid response includes a compliance BitScore (0-100) and a verdict of clear, possible_match or match. kind="signals" is a pre-payment counterparty check that combines the sanctions screen with a reputation BitScore (0-100) and a verdict of do_not_pay, review, ok or unknown. Pass a pay-to (x402/EVM) address, Lightning invoice, LN address, node pubkey, domain, url or business name. Volume packs: 100 checks for 2,000 sats or 1,000 for 15,000 sats at POST /api/v1/credits. A screening aid only, not legal advice or a KYC/AML product; unknown is not a finding that a payee is safe. Pass name and/or address for the sanctions tiers; optional country and dob narrow name matches. An exact address match is definitive. Fuzzy name hits are always a possible match, never a flat yes. Informational only, not legal advice. get_sanctions_data is a deprecated alias of this tool. Returns JSON in the `data` field with source attribution. Read-only; the only side effect is the payment you choose to make.
Kinds and prices:

tools.name: create_feed
tools.description: Use this when an agent would otherwise poll: get data pushed on a schedule (e.g. hourly BTC price) or when a trigger fires (BTC moves 2%, price crosses a level, a weather alert for a location, an airport delay, a new 10-K or 8-K). Delivery is a webhook and/or a 72 h mailbox; each delivery costs the same as one normal call, debited from prepaid credits (fund with buy_credits first); creating a feed is free. Omit credit_token on your first feed to open an account (a btf_ token is returned ONCE: store it). Example: create_feed(endpoint="btc_price", mode="trigger", trigger={"type": "btc_move", "percent": 2})

credit_token.description: Prepaid token (btf_...), returned once by buy_credits or create_feed. Send it on every later feed or credit call.

endpoint.description: Endpoint to deliver: btc_intuitive, btc_stats, btc_pro, btc_signals, weather_intuitive, weather_stats, weather_signals, travel_intuitive, stock_filings or stock_fundamentals (deprecated aliases such as btc_price, btc_oracle, weather_now and airport_delays still work). Put its arguments in `params`.

mode.description: schedule: deliver on an interval. trigger: deliver when the trigger condition hits.

interval.description: mode=schedule: 'hourly', 'daily' or a number of seconds (minimum 900).

interval_seconds.description: mode=schedule: the interval in seconds (alternative to interval).

trigger.description: Required when mode=trigger. type is one of: btc_move (percent, optional window_seconds), btc_threshold (above and/or below, in USD), weather_alert (location), airport_delay (airport, optional min_delay_minutes), sec_filing (symbol, optional forms; default 8-K, 10-Q, 10-K). Optional max_fires, expires_at, cooldown_seconds.

webhook_url.description: https URL to POST deliveries to. A signing secret is returned once.

mailbox.description: Also store deliveries in the mailbox (default true).

tools.name: get_feeds
tools.description: Use this when you need to check your feeds: without feed_id it lists every feed and the prepaid sats balance; with feed_id it returns that feed's status, schedule and next delivery. Read-only. Example: get_feeds(feed_id="...")

credit_token.description: Prepaid token (btf_...), returned once by buy_credits or create_feed. Send it on every later feed or credit call.

tools.name: update_feed
tools.description: Use this when you want to change a feed: interval, trigger, params, webhook_url, mailbox, or pause/resume it with `state`. Only the fields you pass change. Resuming fails if the prepaid balance is zero or the feed expired. No charge. Safe to repeat.

credit_token.description: Prepaid token (btf_...), returned once by buy_credits or create_feed. Send it on every later feed or credit call.

feed_id.description: Feed id returned by create_feed or get_feeds.

state.description: paused stops deliveries; active resumes them.

trigger.description: Required when mode=trigger. type is one of: btc_move (percent, optional window_seconds), btc_threshold (above and/or below, in USD), weather_alert (location), airport_delay (airport, optional min_delay_minutes), sec_filing (symbol, optional forms; default 8-K, 10-Q, 10-K). Optional max_fires, expires_at, cooldown_seconds.

tools.name: delete_feed
tools.description: Use this when you no longer want a feed. PERMANENTLY deletes the feed definition and stops all future deliveries; this cannot be undone (create a new feed to restart). Deliveries already in the mailbox stay until they expire (72 h); the prepaid balance is untouched and non-refundable. Requires the account token and the feed id. Prefer update_feed state=paused if you may want it back.

credit_token.description: Prepaid token (btf_...), returned once by buy_credits or create_feed. Send it on every later feed or credit call.

feed_id.description: Feed id returned by create_feed or get_feeds.

tools.name: get_credit_balance
tools.description: Use this when you want to know how much prepaid balance (sats and USDC) is left before running more calls or feeds. Read-only. Example: get_credit_balance(credit_token="btf_...")

credit_token.description: Prepaid token (btf_...), returned once by buy_credits or create_feed. Send it on every later feed or credit call.

tools.name: buy_credits
tools.description: Use this when you will make many calls or run feeds and want to pay once instead of per call. Omit credit_token to open a new account: the result includes a btf_ token shown ONCE, store it. Lightning: pass bundle or amount_sats (100 to 1,000,000) to get an invoice, pay it, then call again with payment_hash and credit_token to credit it. USDC on Base (x402): pass bundle or amount_usd (0.10 to 50), sign accepts[0], call again with the same amount plus x402_payment; USDC is settled before crediting. Sats pay sats prices, USDC pays USDC list prices; spend with credit_token on any paid tool. Credits are NON-REFUNDABLE; a call that fails is refunded to the balance. Paused feeds resume after credit.

credit_token.description: Prepaid token (btf_...), returned once by buy_credits or create_feed. Send it on every later feed or credit call.

bundle.description: A preset amount; see get_pricing for the sats and USD of each.

amount_sats.description: Lightning: sats to add (100 to 1,000,000). Alternative to bundle.

amount_usd.description: USDC over x402: dollars to add (0.10 to 50), e.g. "1.00".

currency.description: With bundle: which currency to pay in.

x402_payment.description: x402 payment (USDC on Base): base64 PaymentPayload signed for accepts[0] of the payment_required result. Alternative to l402_credential; also accepted in params._meta['x402/payment'].

payment_hash.description: Lightning: check this invoice and credit it if paid, instead of creating a new one.

Items are kept 72 hours. Read-only; hide handled items with ack_feed_mailbox_item. Example: get_feed_mailbox(feed_id="...")

feed_id.description: Optional. Only items from this feed.
